pr_body:
Fix #23448 

`EVP_PKEY_CTX_add1_hkdf_info()` behaves like a `set1` function.

Fix the setting of the parameter in the params code. Update the TLS_PRF code to also use the params code. Add tests.

pr_comments:
concat_octet_string() is used in hkdf, kbkdf, sskdf.
HPKE uses HKDF inside its KEM (eckem.c or ecxkem.c) Which is probably where you are seeing an issue in the test.

> concat_octet_string() is used in hkdf, kbkdf, sskdf. HPKE uses HKDF inside its KEM (eckem.c or ecxkem.c) Which is probably where you are seeing an issue in the test.

My bad was to focus on the `pkey_meth_kdf_test` to the exclusion of all others (i.e. I didn't run them on my machine), and I'm surprised it's behaving this way.

The info/seed result is the same regardless. The basic tests I added have the same result.

The problem with the test is that `kdf_derive()` in kpke_util.c applies `OSSL_KDF_PARAM_INFO` expecting it to _set_ and not _add_, whereas the public API is to _add_. So, perhaps internally, we need to continue to do a set, but the `add1` function performs the add logic by retrieving the old value.
Otherwise, internal uses of HKDF will have to have someway to specify set vs add (and add isn't used), or a way to reset the INFO before adding (setting). Which seems like a mess.

That becomes a spider's web fixes all over the place increasing risk. So I'm now leaning toward updating the public `add1` API instead. Note that the `add1` API for the TLS PRF does concatenation internally, and all users are aware of that.

> So, perhaps internally, we need to continue to do a set, but the `add1` function performs the add logic by retrieving the old value.

Yeah, this needs to be done in the API call and not in the provider implementation.
@slontis and @t8m, I finally got back to getting this fixed.

> Note that if you are doing this in production code you may want to consider switching to the EVP_KDF interface. This is using a legacy bridge since it is not really a key exchange operation (You can see that internally it does extra KDF_fetch() calls - so that will be slower).

(I thought I had replied to this already)

This is purposely generic, and based on the `evp_pkey_ctx_set1_octet_string()` function, which it calls if there's no previously set value.

While this does make `EVP_PKEY_CTX_add1_hkdf_info` behave according to the docs and the function name, it unfortunately leaves `EVP_PKEY_CTX` less reusable, since now it is only possible to add new labels, not set/replace previous labels.

Is there a plan to fill in the rest of this API to allow these hkdf contexts to be reused like they were previously?

> While this does make `EVP_PKEY_CTX_add1_hkdf_info` behave according to the docs and the function name, it unfortunately leaves `EVP_PKEY_CTX` less reusable, since now it is only possible to add new labels, not set/replace previous labels.
> 
> Is there a plan to fill in the rest of this API to allow these hkdf contexts to be reused like they were previously?

You can always use the EVP_PKEY_CTX_set_params() directly and that provides the set/replace semantics. You can get an inspiration how to do that by looking at  evp_pkey_ctx_set1_octet_string() implementation.

Yeah, that is what we ended up doing -- it feels a bit implementation specific, and it would be nice if there was a `set1_hkdf_info` supported in the api, but I understand that introduces compatibility concerns.

issue_context.title: EVP_PKEY_CTX_add1_hkdf_info() behaves like ""_set1_""
issue_context.body:
Per the [man page](https://www.openssl.org/docs/man3.0/man3/EVP_PKEY_CTX_add1_hkdf_info.html), consecutive calls to this function should have the net effect of concatenation:

> EVP_PKEY_CTX_add1_hkdf_info() sets the info value to infolen bytes of the buffer info. If a value is already set, it is appended to the existing value. 

However, this does not appear to be the case. What I have observed to be the case is that only the last call sticks.

A simple reproducer can be constructed by trivially modifying the example code snippet further down in said man page. Simply break up the EVP_PKEY_CTX_add1_hkdf_info(pctx, "label", 5) line across multiple calls (eg, "lab" w/ 3 followed by "el" w/ 2) and compare the output bytes.

As best I can tell, this looks like a regression introduced in 3.0. There seems to be some interface confusion. At least in the 3.0 line, there are couple of places with comments around intending to handle concatenation in providers/implementations/kdfs/hkdf.c... but crypto/evp/pmeth_lib.c seems to be translating add1 into just a set without fetching the existing ones (if any) to pass along as well (as the provider code seems to anticipate).

FWIW, it also looked like some other add1 APIs in pmeth_lib.c (eg, EVP_PKEY_CTX_add1_tls1_prf_seed) may also have the same problem, although I haven't tested them.

review_comments: You will need to check the fips provider version here and skip the index 1 test if an old fips provider is used.
I think I figured it out.
Ideally this would have an expected result after the derive, so that you know it added the info correctly..

It's calling `add1` twice in this portion of the test, vs the `index == 0` case where it calls `add1` once. The values end up being the same, and the `EVP_PKEY_derive()` is at the end where the expected value is compared.

When called with an older provider that does not support OSSL_KDF_PARAM_INFO as gettable, the return_size will be OSSL_PARAM_UNMODIFIED. You need to check that value. However it would be wrong to error out here IMO. Just treat this as if nothing was set before so at least the first evp_pkey_ctx_add1_octet_string() does the right thing.
